office_does: A Thurston PUD commissioner sits on the three-member board of a water utility that runs 271 water systems serving about 25,000 people, adopting its budget and setting rates; this seat is the four-year unexpired remainder of a six-year term.
race_blurb: Appointed Commissioner Jim Campbell, the PUD's former field operations director, is backed by the other two commissioners and his predecessor. Challenger Troy Kirby, a former Lacey parks commissioner, runs on affordability and a critique of the board's fixed charges, PFAS surcharge and emergency bid waivers. All county voters decide the seat.

candidates.summary: Appointed PUD commissioner since October 2025 and former PUD director of field operations, with about 22 years in the water industry after 20 years as an Olympia Brewery foreman.
highlights: Former PUD director of field operations overseeing about 270 water systems; appointed to the board unanimously in September 2025 [S1][S9]
Describes utility management as "infrastructure first, cost second, and safety always" and stresses preventive maintenance [S1]
Recommended a 1.9 percent rate increase for the 2027 budget [S14]
Endorsed by PUD Commissioners Stearns and Olsen and former Commissioner Linda Oosterman [S3]

candidates.summary: State agency communications staffer and seven-year Lacey parks commissioner running on affordable rates, grant and settlement funding for PFAS cleanup, and a critique of the PUD board's fees and bidding.
highlights: Would pay for PFAS cleanup and major projects with state grants, infrastructure funding and polluter settlements [S1]
Fact sheet calls the PUD's $1.78 monthly PFAS surcharge "a tax on the victims, not the polluters" and criticizes fixed charges and emergency bid waivers [S3]
Supports stronger customer assistance programs and open public meetings [S1]
Previously ran for Lacey City Council (2019) and Port of Olympia commissioner (2023) [S5][S6]
